item.title: Hausdorff Matrices on the BMOA and Bloch spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.22554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum of Hausdorff operators $\mathcal{H}_\mu$ on BMOA and the Bloch space $\mathscr{B}$, for suitable finite positive Borel measures $\mu$ on $(0,1]$.
item.dc:creator: Petros Galanopoulos, Alejandro Mahillo, Jesus Oliva-Maza, Aristomenis G. Siskakis

item.title: Embedding theorems for Herz-Type Sobolev spaces on domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.22570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we further investigate the properties of Herz-type Sobolev spaces on domains, which unify and generalize the classical Sobolev spaces. In particular, we establish several Sobolev-type embedding theorems for these spaces. Moreover, by means of a suitable example, we show that some of the assumptions imposed on the parameters are optimal.
item.dc:creator: Douadi Drihem

item.title: A Spectral Approach to Fixed Points in Product Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.22666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fixed points of mappings on finite products of Banach spaces whose coordinatewise Lipschitz estimates are controlled by a nonnegative matrix $A$. Our main result states that, if every coordinate space has normal structure and $r(A)\leq1$, then every such self-mapping of a nonempty weakly compact convex set has a fixed point. The result is a direct generalization of the Browder--G\"ohde--Kirk principle. The proof combines classical nonexpansive fixed point theory with Frobenius normal form, passing successively to coordinate projections and invariant fibres. As preparation, the classical reduction of Perov's theorem to the Banach contraction principle through adapted lattice norms is revisited. Applications include a Dirichlet boundary value problem for systems of abstract second order differential equations and a periodic problem for ODE systems satisfying one-sided matrix estimates.
item.dc:creator: Aleksander \'Cwiszewski, Wojciech Kryszewski

item.title: Universal operators: topology and consequences of ISP failure
item.description: arXiv:2610.22694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming a negative answer to the invariant subspace problem for separable complex Hilbert spaces, we prove that every universal operator has a continuum of minimal infinite-dimensional invariant subspaces with pairwise trivial intersections. These subspaces can be chosen so that the restrictions are invertible and their powers decay at any prescribed geometric rate. For an affine composition operator on the Hardy space \(H^2(\D)\), we derive restrictions on the zeros, inner factors and Hardy regularity of generators, and construct minimal models with radial vanishing of any prescribed finite order. Independently of the invariant subspace problem, we identify the norm interior, closure and boundary of the universal operator class. Its interior is the Caradus--Pozzi class, its closure is the complement of the upper semi-Fredholm class, and its boundary consists of the operators that are neither upper nor lower semi-Fredholm.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Carmo, Ben-Hur Eidt, Waleed Noor

item.title: Compact Toeplitz Operators and the Geometry of Fixed-Radius Averages
item.description: arXiv:2610.22893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize compact Toeplitz operators with bounded complex-valued symbols on the Bergman space of a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain with $C^2$ boundary. For any fixed $R>0$, the operator $T_f$ is compact if and only if the Euclidean-volume averages of $f$ over Bergman geodesic balls of radius $R$ tend to zero at the boundary. This answers Zhu's fixed-radius question affirmatively on the unit ball. On the polydisc $\mathbb D^n$, $n\ge2$, averages over products of Bergman discs of fixed radii characterize compactness, whereas averages over genuine Bergman geodesic balls need not. For every sufficiently small fixed radius, we construct a bounded real-valued symbol, smooth in the domain, whose geodesic-ball averages tend to zero along every sequence approaching the boundary, while its Berezin transform converges to a positive value along one such sequence. Boundary scaling reduces the strongly pseudoconvex case to a uniqueness problem for fixed-radius ball averages on complex hyperbolic space. We prove the required uniqueness theorem under a sharp decay condition expressed in terms of a Busemann height function.
item.dc:creator: Pan Ma, Zhaoxi Zhang

item.title: On Mbekhta's conjecture and pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.23229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give negative answers to Mbekhta's conjecture \cite[p.~261]{Mbekhta} and to a related conjecture on pseudo-B-Fredholm operators \cite[p.~202]{AZO}. A sufficient condition for pseudo-Fredholmness on Banach spaces is established. It yields a characterization on Hilbert spaces in terms of the closedness of $\cc(T)$, $\cc(T)+\qn(T)$ and $\Ran(T)+\qn(T)$, as well as characterizations of pseudo-B-Fredholm and pseudo-B-Weyl operators on Banach spaces. A counterexample on a separable Banach space shows that the three closedness conditions do not characterize pseudo-Fredholmness in general. We also construct two operators having the same analytic core, quasinilpotent part, and kernels and ranges of all powers, although only one is pseudo-Fredholm. Moreover, a semi-B-Fredholm operator on a Banach space need not be a direct sum of a semi-Fredholm operator and a nilpotent operator, answering the question raised in \cite[p.~113]{AznayKato2023}. Finally, the three closedness conditions in the Hilbert-space characterization are shown to be independent.
item.dc:creator: Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi

item.title: Weak$^*$-weak points of continuity and very smooth points in Bochner function spaces $L^{p}(\mu, X)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.23502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Suppose that $([0,1],\mathcal{A},\mu)$ is the Lebesgue measure space and $1< p<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. We prove that an unit vector $h\in L^{p}(\mu, X)^*$ is a weak$^*$-weak point of continuity of $S(L^{p}(\mu, X)^*)$ if and only if $\frac{h(t)}{\|h(t)\|}$ is a weak$^*$-weak point of continuity of $S(X^*)$ for almost every $t\in [0, 1]$ with $h(t)\neq 0$, where $X$ is a Banach space such that $X^*$ is separable. As an application of this result, under the same hypothesis on $X$, we prove that a point $f\in L^p(\mu, X)_{1}$ is a very smooth point if and only if $\frac{f(t)}{\|f(t)\|}\in S(X)$ is a very smooth point for almost every $t\in [0, 1]$ with $f(t)\neq 0$. We give several examples to show that these results does not hold for $p=1$.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Dwivedi

item.title: Strongly Choquet-Deny groups and invariant strictly convex renormings
item.description: arXiv:2610.23584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study a strengthening of the notion of Choquet-Deny groups, which we call \emph{strongly Choquet-Deny groups}. We show that a countable group $G$ is strongly Choquet-Deny if and only if for every uniformly bounded representation of $G$ on any separable Banach space $X$, there exists an equivalent $G$-invariant strictly convex norm on $X$. We provide a full classification of finitely generated strongly Choquet-Deny groups and show that a finitely generated group is strongly Choquet-Deny if and only if it is virtually abelian. This fully resolves a question of Mikael de la Salle for finitely generated groups. As a further application, we show that for every uniformly bounded representation of a compact extension of an abelian topological group on any separable Banach space, there exists an equivalent invariant strictly convex norm.
item.dc:creator: Sheldon Dantas, Michal Doucha

item.title: Reverse Urysohn inequality for functions and functional Shephard problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.23586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The results obtained in this paper provide a generalization of some geometric inequalities to the class of log-concave functions. They describe the relationships between the Quermassintegrals of functions and bodies, giving estimates for constants involved in functional Shephard-type problems.
item.dc:creator: Vadim Gorev

item.title: On the asymptotic growth of the norm of the partial sum operator on $\mathscr H^1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.23666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the norm of the partial sum operator $S_N$ on the Hardy space $\mathscr H^1$ of Dirichlet series satisfies $$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\log N}{\log N}\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\geq\frac{1-\log 2}{2\pi}.$$ Combined with an upper bound of Bondarenko, Brevig, Saksman and Seip, this shows that $$\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\asymp\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}$$ as $N\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Viktor Andersson

item.title: Order relations for the near geometric and near spectral geometric curves
item.dc:creator: Muritala Abiodun Ibrahim, Huajun Huang

item.title: Constructions and reductions on the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate five open problems concerning the Hornich-Hlawka inequality and its generalizations posed by Marinescu and Niculescu. We give constructive answers to three of them. First, we construct an equivalent norm on $\ell^2$ with no three-dimensional Hornich-Hlawka subspace. Second, we present a Nakano space that is not Hornich-Hlawka. Third, we show that the $\alpha$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality fails to hold on nonzero normed spaces when $\alpha \in (1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)$. This implies that on every nonzero inner product space, the $\alpha$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality holds for all triples precisely when $\alpha \in (0,1] \cup \{2\}$. For the remaining two problems, we establish reductions. We prove that $\ell^p(N)$ is Hornich-Hlawka for all $N \geq 3$ and $2 < p \leq \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$ if and only if it is Hornich-Hlawka at $N = 3$ and $p = \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$. Finally, for $p(\cdot): (0, 1) \to [1, 2]$ measurable and integers $k \geq 0$, we establish a Sobolev-Nakano equivalence: we prove that $W^{k,p(\cdot)}(0,1)$, equipped with the sum of the Luxemburg norms of its derivatives of orders $0, \ldots, k$, is Hornich-Hlawka if and only if $L^{p(\cdot)}(0,1)$ is Hornich-Hlawka.
item.dc:creator: Seokbin Lee

item.title: Hardy-Sobolev-Maz'ya Inequalities for $\boldsymbol{1<p<2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.22540v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$ for singularities supported on affine subspaces and for arbitrary domains. We first prove a Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality for singularities supported on affine subspaces of arbitrary codimension $1\leq k<N$, showing that the deficit in the sharp Hardy inequality controls a suitable weighted Sobolev norm. Combining the same convexity estimate with the one-dimensional approach of Frank and Loss in [9], we also establish Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on arbitrary domains with the mean distance to the boundary and thereby solve a problem posed in [9]. These results complete the previously unresolved subquadratic range $1<p<2$ and, together with the known results for $p\geq 2$, provide a unified Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya theory for all $1<p<N$ associated with plane singularities and general domains.
item.dc:creator: Avas Banerjee, Micha{\l} Kijaczko, Vivek Sahu

item.title: Double interaction principle for the Lorentz force equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.22627v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study the Lorentz force equation using the Poincare action functional. We show that, if the scalar electric potential has good interactions at infinity and around the origin with the vector magnetic potential, then the Lorentz force equation has at least two periodic solutions with a fixed period. For the proof of our main result we introduce a new minimax theorem for the Poincare action functional that does not require the Palais-Smale compactness condition and provides the existence of twin critical points. The interaction at infinity in the electromagnetic potential implies a weak compactness property of the Poincare action functional, while the interaction around the origin gives the separation property of the functional.
item.dc:creator: Cristain Bereanu, Nicusor Costea

item.title: Anomalies for compact simple Lie groups via $G$-kernels for loop group nets
item.description: arXiv:2610.23321v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a compact simply connected simple Lie group and $k \geq 1$. Jump loops give an outer homomorphism $\theta_k$ from $G$ to the outer automorphisms of the local factor of the level-$k$ loop group net, which is the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor. We show that its Sutherland obstruction is $k$ times the positive basic class in $H^3_{\mathrm{Borel}}(G, \mathbb{T}) \cong H^{4}(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ and that $\theta_k$ is faithful, so it is a $G$-kernel. Central elements act by the outer automorphisms of the simple currents. In types A, D, E the level-one class is computed by comparing maximal-torus jump loops with the lattice $\alpha$-induction construction of the companion paper on both current and charged generators, followed by integral degree-four Cartan restriction. Higher levels follow by tensor additivity, and the remaining types by restriction along index-one embeddings into simply laced groups. As a consequence, for every compact simply connected semisimple $G$, every class in $H^4(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ is the obstruction of a $G$-kernel on the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor.
item.dc:creator: Marcel Bischoff, Pradyut Karmakar

item.title: Non-linear Dirichlet Functionals: Markovianity, Locality, Invariance
item.description: arXiv:2510.02942v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present in a unified setting the foundations for a theory of non-linear Dirichlet functionals on Hilbert spaces. We prove known and new equivalences between non-linear semigroups, non-linear resolvents, non-linear generators, and their energy functionals, including a complete characterization of Markovianity. We introduce and characterize strong notions of invariance for general lower semicontinuous convex functionals, and notions of locality and strong locality for non-linear Dirichlet functionals. Contrary to many partial results in the literature, these characterizations are complete under minimal natural assumptions, and reduce to the classical ones in the bilinear case. Our definitions and proofs simplify and clarify the analogous facts in the linear theory, showing in particular that (the equality defining) locality is a saturation of (the inequality defining) Markovianity.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Brigati, Lorenzo Dello Schiavo

item.title: L\"{o}wner equations and de Branges--Rovnyak spaces
item.description: arXiv:2512.10368v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study one-parameter families of de Branges--Rovnyak spaces associated with the radial and chordal L\"{o}wner equations. Our approach is based on a classical but little-known technique of the de Branges school. In this paper, we recast this technique in the theory of direct integrals and integral operators. As an application, we prove Fourier-type expansion theorems induced by the L\"{o}wner equations, and give answers to a problem posed by Fricain--Hartmann--Ross.
item.dc:creator: Michio Seto

item.title: Compact embeddings of variable exponent Sobolev, Besov, and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces on metric measure spaces
item.description: arXiv:2603.23671v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study compact embeddings of Sobolev, Besov, and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces with variable exponents on both bounded and unbounded metric measure spaces. We establish sufficient conditions for compactness, and under additional assumptions, we show that they are also necessary. Moreover, we investigate the influence of isometry group actions on the compactness of embeddings. In particular, we answer the open question posed by P. G\'orka in [P. G\'orka, Looking For Compactness In Sobolev Spaces On Noncompact etric Spaces, Ann. Acad. Sci. Fenn., Vol 43, 2018, 531-540], proving a Berestycki-Lions type theorem.
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Dymek

item.title: On one relaxation of the bounded-length-distortion condition in the context of metric measure spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.00278v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We reformulate the bounded-length-distortion condition for maps between metric spaces in a certain relaxed form that requires the presence of a reference measure on the source space, which makes the new approach more natural from the perspective of maps from metric measure spaces to metric spaces. Within this framework, we establish some mapping results in an entirely singular setting of the following general structure: a metric measure space of finite Hausdorff dimension admits a map with the relaxed bounded-length-distortion condition into a finite-dimensional normed space.
item.dc:creator: Roman D. Oleinik

item.title: Banach Gelfand Triples with Kernel Theorems via Equivalence Bimodules
item.description: arXiv:2609.37780v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hilbert C*-modules whose coefficient C*-algebra is equipped with a finite faithful trace generate Banach Gelfand triples. This provides a natural setting for the interpretation of Hilbert C*-modules as function spaces. In particular, when the modules are finitely generated and projective, their external tensor products interact well with projective tensor products. This allowed us to derive abstract kernel theorems for Hilbert C*-modules. As an application, we apply our results to Heisenberg modules and obtain new kernel theorems for time-frequency analysis.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Bytchenkoff, Arvin Lamando, Franz Luef

item.title: Kadison-Kastler Distance and Interior Angle for Masas: Connections with Entropy and Probabilistic Index
item.description: arXiv:2609.38206v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Kadison--Kastler distance and the interior angle between masas in finite-dimensional matrix algebras. In \(\mathbb{M}_2(\mathbb{C})\), we obtain an explicit formula for the Kadison--Kastler distance between two masas and show that every value in \([0,1]\) is attained by \(\mathrm{d}_{\textrm{KK}}(\Delta,u\Delta u^*)\). We further prove that the distance attains its maximal value precisely when the relative unitary is a Hadamard unitary. In addition, for every $v$ in the groupoid normaliser of $\Delta$, the Kadison--Kastler distance between \(\Delta\) and \(v\Delta v^*\) assumes either its minimal or maximal possible value. We also establish the identity \[ \mathrm{d}_{\textrm{KK}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})=\sin\alpha(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) \] for any two intermediate subalgebras \(\mathbb{C}\subsetneq\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\subsetneq\mathbb{M}_2(\mathbb{C})\). Most notably, for any unitaries \(u,v\in\mathbb{M}_2(\mathbb{C})\), we establish the equivalence of maximal Kadison--Kastler distance, maximal interior angle, maximal Connes--St\o rmer modified entropy, and minimal Popa probabilistic index: \[ \mathrm{d}_{\textrm{KK}}(u\Delta u^*,v\Delta v^*)=1 \iff h(u\Delta u^*,v\Delta v^*)=\log 2 \iff \alpha(u\Delta u^*,v\Delta v^*)=\frac{\pi}{2} \iff \lambda(u\Delta u^*,v\Delta v^*)=\frac{1}{2}. \] For general \(\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})\), we prove a unitary invariance property for the interior angle and derive an explicit formula for the angle between arbitrary masas of the form \(u\Delta^{(n)}u^*\) and \(v\Delta^{(n)}v^*\). As a consequence, the interior angle is \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) precisely when the relative unitary \(u^*v\) is a Hadamard unitary. Finally, we show that every value in \(\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) is attained as the interior angle between a pair of masas in \(\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})\).
item.dc:creator: Indrajit Ghosh, Sumit Kumar

item.title: A Rockafellar theorem for cyclically quasi-monotone maps: The regular non-vanishing case
item.description: arXiv:2507.09437v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the connection between cyclic quasi-monotonicity and quasi-convexity, focusing on whether every cyclically quasi-monotone (possibly multi-valued) map is included in the normal cone operator of a quasi-convex function, in analogy with Rockafellar's theorem for convex functions. We provide a positive answer for locally Lipschitz, non-vanishing maps in any dimension, as well as for general multi-maps in dimension $1$. We further discuss connections to revealed preference theory in economics and to $L^\infty$ optimal transport. Finally, we present explicit constructions and examples, highlighting the main challenges that arise in the general case.
item.dc:creator: Luigi De Pascale, Paul Pegon

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.12908v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A bipartite observable is stable when its expectation does not depend on which system is idealized first. We show that it is stable exactly when its idealized responses are continuous, and NIP exactly when they are of the first Baire class. For a NIP observable the idealized responses form a Rosenthal compactum, and the dividing lines of Shelah in model theory, together with the classification of Rosenthal compacta of Todor\v{c}evi\'c, acquire a physical meaning. We prove that, for observables, mixtures of states make every hereditarily separable compactum of idealized responses metrizable. The Todor\v{c}evi\'c trichotomy thus becomes a classification into three classes, and we exhibit in each class a physical order: the comparison of photon numbers, the comparison of positions, and the causal order of spacetime, whose idealized responses are not first countable because a light cone can shrink to a point; the comparison of two phases on a circle joins the causal order in the third class. Each of the seven minimal families of the heptachotomy, which Argyros, Dodos and Kanellopoulos extracted from the methods of Todor\v{c}evi\'c, is realized, as we show, by a tree of preparations of photons, of a particle in a box, or of a spin chain read by a probe; the spin chain also reveals that NIP, unlike its uniform version, is not symmetric between the two parties. Finally, for the Ising model in a transverse field we prove that, in the ordered phase, the responses of the two pure phases form split pairs whose midpoints, the responses of the symmetric state, form an uncountable discrete set; the proof rests on a Lee--Yang theorem for this model.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino
